source.title: What can linear interpolation of neural network loss landscapes tell us?

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a ResNet-18 that first fits random labels can subsequently achieve high test accuracy after standard training on natural labels; it does not test the random-label held-out accuracy condition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-label pretraining followed by CIFAR-10 training and final test accuracy. Its other results concern interpolation-path shape and test accuracy, not the mapped claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study extends V1 to ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10: it fits random labels to 100% training accuracy and subsequently achieves 89.7% natural-label test accuracy. This tests coexistence in a sequential-training setting, but not random-label held-out performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes one initialization result but misses the main conclusion: initial-to-final linear interpolation shape is not a reliable indicator of test accuracy. The authors also find layer-dependent sensitivity to initialization and learning rates, and that partial pretraining can lower final accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The model is first trained to fit random labels, then used as the initialization for CIFAR-10 training; the reported setting omits weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight decay: the reported natural-label test-accuracy decrease after random-label pretraining is in the no-weight-decay setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear interpolation barriers between initial and final weights do not reliably predict final test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial-to-final interpolation-path shape is not a reliable predictor of test accuracy. This does not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation measure or generalization-gap ranking.

fits_no_version.finding: The spiral-data MLP width variants in Figure A17 all achieve 100% test accuracy; Table A4 reports test accuracy after selectively narrowing VGG-11 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width changes can alter interpolation barriers or test accuracy, but these experiments do not establish continued test-error reduction beyond a measured zero-training-error width threshold as V2 requires.

fits_no_version.finding: Block-wise random-label initialization produces natural-label test accuracies that depend on the transferred block and weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transferring individual blocks from a random-label-trained network affects subsequent generalization. These partially initialized networks are not shown themselves to fit random labels, so this does not independently establish V1.

record.problems: The random-label held-out accuracy is not reported, so the paper does not establish that it remains at chance. The reported result is limited to ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 without weight decay.
record.rows_left_out: No other result reports the combination of random-label fitting and subsequent natural-label test accuracy in a way that bears on V1.

untested.parts: Held-out accuracy with random labels; the original architectures and recipes without explicit regularization; and a matched comparison of independent natural-label and random-label training from random initialization.

record.verdict_notes: The 0.3 percentage-point decrease after random-label pretraining does not challenge V1: natural-label accuracy remains far above chance. Neither interpolation barriers nor weight-decay effects alone test the other listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy on random labels or test the full set of architectures and training recipes in the version.

rows.subject: ResNet-18

rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 after pretraining on 100% random labels until 100% training accuracy
rows.note: The paper states that random-label pretraining reaches 100% training accuracy; held-out random-label accuracy is not reported.
rows.check: The numbers and baseline match Figure 2B. Correct the section locator to Section 4, Adversarial initialization. The natural-label recipe also uses batch normalization and data augmentation; omitting weight decay does not reproduce the original unregularized recipe. Results are averaged over 10 runs, although numerical uncertainty is not supplied for this comparison.
